summary: Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Central Hindu College (c. 1899–1914) and headmaster at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (c. 1921–1940).

Working in Indology and linguistics, Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he was attested in 1976 and served as head of the Research Department as attested in 1989.

Bhagwan Dash worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, where he earned a PhD (c. 1973–1978). He served as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was an honorary member of the Royal Asiatic Society (1877), a member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (c. 1877–1888), and a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (1882).

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Bhajagobinda Ghosh was attested in 1994 as an editorial board member of the Bulletin of Tibetology and as assistant director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra, and held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhaskar Anand Saletore specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Henry Heras and doctoral supervisor Lionel David Barnett, and served as Professor of History at Sir Parashurambhau College (attested 1936).

Bhau Daji was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Elphinstone College (c. 1840–1845) and Grant Medical College and Sir Jamshedjee Jeejeebhoy Group of Hospitals (c. 1845–1851).

Bhikkhu Anālayo worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Peradeniya and a Habilitation at the University of Marburg, and held posts at the University of Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute, SIBA, and Barre Center.

Bhikkhu Bodhi specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Brooklyn College and a Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University. His posts include editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States (2013).

Bhikkhu Pāsādika is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar with degrees from Magadh University and Punjabi University. His posts include lecturing at Punjabi University, University of Marburg, and University of Würzburg, as well as positions at the Göttingen Academy and Frankfurt Buddhist Academy.
Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā, a scholar of Buddhist studies, completed her PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007). She studied under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, as well as Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

Bhogilal Sandesara, an Indologist and linguist, studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (c. 1958–1975), and was Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (c. 1951–1975).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi, who worked in Indology and other fields, studied at Patna University. He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of California, Santa Cruz, where he was a professor (c. 1969–1977).

Bidia Dandaron worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University of Civil Aviation and Saint Petersburg State University, and under Andrei Vostrikov and Lubsan Sandan Tsydenov. He held posts at the Buryat Institute of Social Sciences and IMBTS.

Bihani Sarkar is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held a post at the University of Hamburg and serves as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University (attested 2026).

Bill M. Mak works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He was Associate Professor at Kyoto University (2014–2019), Research Fellow at Needham Research Institute (2019), and held appointments at USTC (Professor, 2024) and the University of Hamburg (Research Fellow, attested 2026).

Bimal Krishna Matilal was an Indologist and philosopher educated at the University of Calcutta and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as Professor at the University of Toronto (c. 1968–1976) and Spalding Professor at the University of Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Patna University and earned his Ph.D. from the University of London under Lionel David Barnett. He headed the department at Patna University (1958) and was Joint Director at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute.
